translation: Those who constantly practice My teachings with full faith and without envy are freed from the bondage of their actions.

title: Chapter 9, Verse 27

title: Chapter 9, Verse 34
translation: Fix your mind on Me, become My devotee, worship Me, and offer your respect to Me. In this way, with your mind fully absorbed in Me and devoted to Me as the supreme goal, you will come to Me.

title: Chapter 10, Verse 4

title: Chapter 12, Verse 13

title: Chapter 12, Verse 17

title: Chapter 13, Verse 10

title: Chapter 13, Verse 6

title: Chapter 13, Verse 7

title: Chapter 9, Verse 4

title: Chapter 13, Verse 3

title: Chapter 13, Verse 31

title: Chapter 5, Verse 17

title: Chapter 4, Verse 10

title: Chapter 12, Verse 6

title: Chapter 12, Verse 8
translation: Fix your mind on Me alone and place your intelligence in Me. Then you will live in Me always, without any doubt.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 9
translation: If you are unable to steadily fix your mind on Me, then try to reach Me through the practice of repeated discipline, O Arjuna.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 11
translation: Constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, aspiring to live in a solitary place, and detachment from the general mass of people.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 26
translation: And one who serves Me with unswerving devotion transcends these three modes of nature and becomes eligible to attain the level of the Supreme.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 19

translation: The Blessed Lord said: Again, O mighty-armed Arjuna, hear My supreme words. Because you are dear to Me, I will speak what is for your highest welfare.

translation: O Krishna, I accept as true everything You have told me. Neither the gods nor the demons fully understand Your true nature.

translation: Among those who enforce discipline I am the power of punishment; among those who seek victory I am wise policy. Among secrets I am silence, and among the knowledgeable I am knowledge itself.

title: Chapter 10, Verse 42

title: Chapter 10, Verse 5

title: Chapter 10, Verse 8
translation: I am the source of everything, and from Me all creation proceeds. Knowing this, the wise worship Me with deep devotion and understanding.

title: Chapter 10, Verse 9
translation: With their minds fixed on Me and their lives devoted to Me, the wise enlighten one another and constantly speak about Me. In doing so, they experience satisfaction and deep joy.

translation: Seeing Your form touching the sky, shining with many colors, with wide open mouths and blazing eyes, my inner self trembles with fear. O Vishnu, I find no steadiness or peace of mind.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 25
translation: Seeing Your terrifying mouths with dreadful fangs, blazing like the fires of destruction, I lose all sense of direction and find no peace. O Lord of the gods, O refuge of the universe, please be graci

title: Chapter 11, Verse 28
translation: Just as many rushing rivers flow toward the ocean, so too these great warriors of the human world are entering Your blazing mouths.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 29
translation: Just as moths rush swiftly into a blazing fire to their destruction, so too all these people are rushing with great speed into Your mouths for their own destruction.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 30
translation: O Vishnu, You are licking and devouring all the worlds from every side with Your blazing mouths. Your fierce radiance fills the entire universe and scorches it with its intense heat.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 32
translation: The Supreme Lord said: I am Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, engaged here in destroying these people. Even without your participation, none of the warriors standing on the opposing side will surv

title: Chapter 11, Verse 33
translation: Therefore arise and gain glory. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. These warriors have already been slain by Me. O skilled archer, you are merely an instrument in this process.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 34
translation: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and many other great warriors have already been slain by Me. Therefore defeat them and do not be disturbed. Fight, and you will conquer your enemies in battle.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 35
translation: Sanjaya said: Hearing these words of Keshava, Arjuna, trembling and with folded hands, bowed down to Krishna. Overwhelmed with fear, he again spoke to Him with a faltering voice.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 36
translation: Arjuna said: O Hrishikesha, it is fitting that the world rejoices and becomes devoted upon hearing Your glories. The demons flee in fear in all directions, while the hosts of perfected beings bow down

title: Chapter 11, Verse 37
translation: O great soul, why should they not bow to You? You are greater even than Brahma, the original creator. O infinite Lord of the gods, refuge of the universe, You are the imperishable reality beyond both

title: Chapter 11, Verse 42
translation: And if, in jest, I have ever shown You disrespect while playing, resting, sitting together, or eating, whether alone or in the presence of others, O Achyuta, I ask Your forgiveness for all of it, O im

title: Chapter 11, Verse 45
translation: Seeing this form which I had never seen before, I am filled with joy, yet my mind is also greatly disturbed with fear. Therefore, O Lord of the gods, O refuge of the universe, please show me again You

title: Chapter 11, Verse 48
translation: O best of the Kurus, this form of Mine that you have seen cannot be perceived in the human world by studying the Vedas, performing sacrifices, giving charity, engaging in rituals, or practicing severe

title: Chapter 11, Verse 49
translation: Do not be afraid or confused after seeing this terrifying form of Mine. Free from fear and with a peaceful mind, behold again My familiar form.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 50
translation: Sanjaya said: After speaking in this way to Arjuna, Vasudeva again showed His own gentle form. The great soul then comforted the frightened Arjuna by appearing once more in His calm and pleasing appea

title: Chapter 11, Verse 53
translation: I cannot be seen in this form as you have seen Me simply through studying the Vedas, performing austerities, giving charity, or conducting sacrifices.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 54
translation: But by undivided devotion, O Arjuna, I can truly be known, seen in reality, and entered into. Through such devotion one can understand Me as I am, O conqueror of enemies.

title: Chapter 11, Verse 55
translation: One who performs actions for Me, who regards Me as the supreme goal, who is devoted to Me, free from attachment, and free from hostility toward all beings, such a person comes to Me, O Arjuna.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 10
translation: If you are unable even to practice steady discipline, then dedicate your actions to Me. By performing actions for My sake, you will attain perfection.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 11
translation: If you are unable to act for My sake, then practice renouncing the results of all your actions with self-control.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 12
translation: Knowledge is better than mechanical practice, meditation is superior to knowledge, and renouncing the results of actions is greater than meditation. From such renunciation, peace immediately follows.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 13
translation: One who has no hatred toward any being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, balanced in both happiness and distress, and forgiving in nature, is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 14
translation: One who is always content, self-disciplined, firmly determined, and whose mind and intellect are dedicated to Me, such a devotee is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 15
translation: One by whom the world is not disturbed and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from excessive joy, anger, fear, and agitation, such a person is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 16
translation: One who is free from expectation, pure in conduct, skillful in action, impartial, free from anxiety, and who has renounced selfish undertakings, such a devotee is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 17
translation: One who neither becomes overly joyful nor hates, neither laments nor desires, and who has renounced attachment to both good and bad outcomes, such a devoted person is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 18
translation: One who remains equal toward friend and enemy, balanced in honor and dishonor, and steady in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, free from attachment, such a person is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 19
translation: One who regards praise and criticism equally, who is thoughtful and restrained in speech, content with whatever comes, unattached to fixed possessions or residence, steady in mind and devoted, such a

title: Chapter 12, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me and constantly worship Me with deep faith are considered by Me to be the most perfectly united in yoga.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 3
translation: But those who worship the imperishable, indefinable, unmanifest reality, which is all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, immovable, and eternal, also engage in a path of spiritual discipline.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 4
translation: Those who control their senses, remain balanced in all situations, and are dedicated to the welfare of all beings also ultimately reach Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 6
translation: But those who dedicate all their actions to Me, who regard Me as their supreme goal, and who worship Me while meditating on Me with single-minded focus, follow a path of devotion.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 7
translation: For those whose minds are fully absorbed in Me, O Arjuna, I become their deliverer from the ocean of birth and death, and I quickly lift them out of the cycle of worldly existence.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 8
translation: Fix your mind on Me alone and place your intelligence in Me. Then you will live in Me always, without any doubt.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 9
translation: If you are unable to steadily fix your mind on Me, then try to reach Me through the practice of repeated discipline, O Arjuna.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 1
translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, I wish to understand Prakriti (nature) and Purusha (the enjoyer), as well as the field and the knower of the field, along with knowledge and the object of knowledge.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 11
translation: Constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, aspiring to live in a solitary place, and detachment from the general mass of people.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 12
translation: Accepting the importance of self-realization, and the philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I declare to be knowledge, and besides this whatever there may be is ignorance.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field (kshetra), and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field (kshetrajna) by those who understand these things.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 21
translation: Material nature (Prakriti) is said to be the cause of all material activities and effects, whereas the conscious entity (Purusha) is the cause of the various experiences of happiness and distress.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 24
translation: One who understands this philosophy concerning material nature, the living entity, and the interaction of the modes of nature is sure to attain liberation. He will not take birth here again, regardles

title: Chapter 13, Verse 25
translation: Some perceive the Supersoul within themselves through meditation, others through the cultivation of knowledge, and still others through working without fruitive desires.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 30
translation: One who can see that all activities are performed by the body, which is a creation of material nature, and sees that the self does nothing, actually sees.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 34
translation: O son of Bharata, as the sun alone illuminates all this universe, so does the living entity, one within the body, illuminate the entire body by consciousness.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 35
translation: Those who see with eyes of knowledge the difference between the body and the knower of the body, and who can also understand the process of liberation from bondage in material nature, attain to the su

title: Chapter 13, Verse 6
translation: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifest, the ten senses and the mind, and the five objects of the senses.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 7
translation: Desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 1
translation: The Supreme Lord said: I shall again reveal to you the supreme wisdom, the best of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages have attained the highest perfection.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 12
translation: O chief of the Bharatas, when the mode of passion increases, the symptoms of greed, intense outward activity, the undertaking of selfish projects, severe restlessness, and uncontrollable craving devel

title: Chapter 14, Verse 14
translation: When an embodied soul passes away while the mode of goodness is predominant, it attains the pure, higher worlds of those who know the Supreme.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 16
translation: The result of righteous action is said to be pure and in the mode of goodness. But action done in the mode of passion results in misery, and action performed in the mode of ignorance results in delusi

title: Chapter 14, Verse 18
translation: Those situated in the mode of goodness go upward; those in the mode of passion remain in the middle; and those in the abominable mode of ignorance go downward.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 19
translation: When one properly sees that in all activities no other performer is at work than these modes of nature, and knows the Supreme who is beyond all these modes, they attain My spiritual nature.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 23
translation: Seated like an unconcerned witness, one who is not disturbed by the material modes, who remains firm and does not waver, knowing that only the modes are active...

title: Chapter 14, Verse 26
translation: And one who serves Me with unswerving devotion transcends these three modes of nature and becomes eligible to attain the level of the Supreme.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 3
translation: The total material nature is My womb. I place the seed of life within it, and from this, O descendant of Bharata, all living beings are born.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 7
translation: O son of Kunti, know that the mode of passion is characterized by intense craving, born of unlimited desires and longings. It binds the embodied soul through attachment to the results of action.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 9
translation: O son of Bharata, the mode of goodness conditions one to happiness; passion conditions one to fruitive action; and ignorance, covering one's knowledge, binds one to negligence and delusion.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 13
translation: I enter into each planet, and by My energy, they stay in orbit. I become the moon and thereby supply the juice of life to all vegetables.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 17
translation: Besides these two, there is the greatest living personality, the Supreme Soul, the imperishable Lord Himself, who has entered the three worlds and is maintaining them.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 2
translation: The branches of this tree extend downward and upward, nourished by the three modes of material nature. The twigs are the objects of the senses. This tree also has roots going down, and these are bound

title: Chapter 15, Verse 20
translation: This most confidential part of the revealed scriptures has been disclosed by Me, O sinless one. Whoever understands this will become wise, and his endeavors will know perfection.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 12
translation: Bound by hundreds of ties of hope and devoted to lust and anger, they strive to accumulate wealth by illegal or unjust means for the satisfaction of their senses.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 16
translation: Thus perplexed by various anxieties and bound by a network of illusions, they become too strongly attached to sense enjoyment and fall down into hell.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 19
translation: Those who are envious and mischievous, who are the lowest among men, I perpetually cast into the ocean of material existence, into various demoniac species of life.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 20
translation: Attaining repeated birth amongst the species of demoniac life, O son of Kunti, such persons can never approach Me. Gradually they sink down to the most abominable type of existence.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 24
translation: Therefore, the scriptures are your authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known the rules and regulations prescribed by the scriptures, you should perform

title: Chapter 16, Verse 6
translation: O son of Pritha, in this world there are two kinds of created beings. One is called the divine and the other demoniac. I have already explained at length the divine qualities. Now hear from Me of the

title: Chapter 16, Verse 7
translation: Those who are demoniac do not know what is to be done and what is not to be done. Neither cleanliness nor proper behavior nor truth is found in them.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 9
translation: Following such conclusions, the demoniac persons, who are lost to themselves and who have no intelligence, engage in unbeneficial, horrible works meant to destroy the world.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 11
translation: Of sacrifices, the sacrifice performed according to the directions of scripture, as a matter of duty, by those who desire no reward, is of the nature of goodness.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 12
translation: O chief of the Bharatas, know that the sacrifice performed with an eye on the fruit, and for the sake of pride, is of the nature of passion.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 13
translation: Any sacrifice performed without regard for the directions of scripture, without distribution of prasadam (spiritual food), without chanting of hymns and remunerations to the priests, and without faith

title: Chapter 17, Verse 14
translation: Austerity of the body consists in worship of the Supreme Lord, the wise, the spiritual master, and superiors like the father and mother, and in cleanliness, simplicity, celibacy and nonviolence.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 16
translation: And satisfaction, simplicity, gravity, self-control and purification of one's existence are the austerities of the mind.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 21
translation: But charity performed with the expectation of some return, or with a desire for fruits, or in a grudging mood, is said to be in the mode of passion.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 23
translation: From the beginning of creation, the three words 'Om Tat Sat' have been used to indicate the Supreme Ultimate Reality. These three symbolic representations were used by the knowers of the Absolute whil

title: Chapter 17, Verse 24
translation: Therefore, by uttering the word 'Om', the acts of sacrifice, charity and penance, as enjoined in the scriptures, are always begun by the students of the Absolute.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 25
translation: One should perform various kinds of sacrifice, penance and charity with the word 'Tat' and without desiring the results. Such activities are performed by those who seek liberation from material entang

title: Chapter 17, Verse 26
translation: The word 'Sat' is used in the sense of the ultimate reality and in the sense of goodness. O Arjuna, the word 'Sat' is also used for an auspicious action.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 27
translation: The state of steadfastness in sacrifice, penance and charity is also called 'Sat,' and any work performed for the sake of the Supreme is also designated as 'Sat.'

title: Chapter 17, Verse 28
translation: Anything done as sacrifice, charity or penance without faith, O son of Pritha, is declared as 'asat.' It is useless both in this life and the next.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 3
translation: O descendant of Bharata, the faith of all beings is in accordance with their nature. A person is made of their faith; as their faith is, so they are.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 8
translation: Foods that increase longevity, virtue, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction are characteristic of the mode of goodness. Such foods are juicy, fatty, wholesome, and pleasing to the heart.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 1
translation: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, I wish to understand the true nature of renunciation (sannyasa) and of detachment (tyaga), and the distinction between the two, O Hrishikesha, killer of the Kesi demon

title: Chapter 18, Verse 10
translation: The intelligent renouncer, situated in the mode of goodness, neither hates inauspicious work nor is attached to auspicious work. Such a person is completely free from all doubts.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 11
translation: It is indeed impossible for an embodied being to give up all activities completely. But one who renounces the fruits of action is called a true renouncer.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 12
translation: The threefold fruits of action—undesirable, desirable, and mixed—accrue after death to those who are attached to the results. But for those who have renounced the fruits of action, there are no such c

title: Chapter 18, Verse 13
translation: O mighty-armed Arjuna, learn from Me the five factors for the accomplishment of all actions, as declared in the Sankhya philosophy, which is the ultimate conclusion of all action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 14
translation: The place of action (the body), the performer (the ego), the various instruments (the senses), the many different kinds of endeavor, and ultimately the Supreme Will (unseen destiny) are the five facto

title: Chapter 18, Verse 15
translation: Whatever right or wrong action a man performs by body, mind or speech, is caused by these five factors.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 17
translation: One who is free from the ego of being the doer, and whose intelligence is not entangled, even though he may slay all these people, he does not kill, nor is he bound by the consequences of the action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 18
translation: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower—these three are the motivating forces of action. The instrument, the action, and the doer—these three are the constituents of action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 19
translation: According to the three different modes of material nature, there are three kinds of knowledge, action, and performer of action. Now hear of them from Me.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Giving up activities based on material desire is what learned men call sannyasa (renunciation). And giving up the results of all activities is what the wise call tyaga (detachme

title: Chapter 18, Verse 20
translation: That knowledge by which one undivided spiritual nature is seen in all living entities, though they are divided into innumerable forms, you should understand to be in the mode of goodness (Sattvic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 22
translation: And that knowledge which is blindly attached to one single activity or concept as if it were everything, without reason, devoid of truth, and which is very narrow and meager, is declared to be in the

title: Chapter 18, Verse 23
translation: That action which is regulated and performed without attachment, without love or hatred, and without desire for fruitive results is said to be in the mode of goodness (Sattvic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 24
translation: But action performed with great effort by one seeking to gratify their desires, and enacted from a sense of false ego, is called action in the mode of passion (Rajasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 25
translation: That action which is undertaken out of delusion, completely disregarding future consequences, loss, injury to others, and one's own capability, is said to be in the mode of ignorance (Tamasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 26
translation: The worker who is free from all material attachments and false ego, who is endowed with great enthusiasm and determination, and who is unperturbed in success or failure, is said to be a worker in the

title: Chapter 18, Verse 27
translation: The worker who is attached to work and the fruits of work, desiring to enjoy those fruits, and who is greedy, always envious, impure, and moved by joy and sorrow, is said to be a worker in the mode of

title: Chapter 18, Verse 28
translation: The worker who is undisciplined, vulgar, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, morose and procrastinating is said to be a worker in the mode of ignorance (Tamasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 29
translation: O winner of wealth, now please listen as I tell you in detail of the three kinds of understanding and determination according to the three modes of material nature.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 3
translation: Some learned men declare that all kinds of fruitive activities should be given up as faulty, yet other sages maintain that acts of sacrifice, charity and penance should never be abandoned.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 30
translation: O son of Pritha, that understanding by which one knows what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, what is to be feared and what is not to be feared, what is binding and what is liberating, i

title: Chapter 18, Verse 31
translation: O son of Pritha, that understanding which cannot distinguish between right and wrong, between action that should be done and action that should not be done, is in the mode of passion (Rajasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 33
translation: O son of Pritha, that determination which is unswerving, which is sustained with steadfastness by yoga practice, and which thus controls the activities of the mind, life and senses, is in the mode of

title: Chapter 18, Verse 34
translation: But that determination by which one holds fast to duty, pleasure, and wealth, desiring the fruits of actions out of intense attachment, O Partha, is in the mode of passion (Rajasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 36
translation: O best among the Bharatas, now please hear from Me about the three kinds of happiness which the conditioned soul enjoys, and by which one sometimes comes to the end of all suffering.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 37
translation: That happiness which is like poison in the beginning but like nectar in the end, and which arises from the purification of one’s own intelligence, is said to be in the mode of goodness (Sattvic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 38
translation: That happiness which is derived from the contact of the senses with their objects and which appears like nectar at first but poison at the end is said to be in the mode of passion (Rajasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 39
translation: That happiness which is blind to self-realization, which is delusion from beginning to end and which arises from sleep, laziness and illusion is said to be of the nature of ignorance (Tamasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 4
translation: O best of the Bharatas, now hear My conclusive judgment concerning renunciation. O tiger among men, renunciation is declared in the scriptures to be of three kinds.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 40
translation: There is no being on earth, or even among the demigods in the higher planetary systems, who is freed from these three modes born of material nature.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 42
translation: Peacefulness, self-control, austerity, purity, tolerance, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and religiousness—these are the natural qualities by which the Brahmins work.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 45
translation: By following his qualities of work, every man can become perfect. Now please hear from Me how this can be done.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 49
translation: One whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has conquered the self, and who is free from desires, attains by renunciation the supreme state of perfection consisting of freedom from action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 5
translation: Acts of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up; they must be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity and penance purify even the great souls.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 50
translation: Learn from Me in brief, O son of Kunti, how one who has attained this perfection can reach the supreme state of Brahman, the highest stage of knowledge.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 51
translation: Being purified by intelligence and controlling the mind with determination, giving up the objects of sense gratification, and casting aside attachment and hatred...

title: Chapter 18, Verse 54
translation: One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments or desires to have anything. He is equally disposed toward every living entity

title: Chapter 18, Verse 56
translation: Though performing all kinds of actions, one who takes shelter in Me reaches the eternal and imperishable state by My grace.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 57
translation: Mentally dedicating all your actions to Me, regarding Me as the Supreme Goal and taking shelter of the yoga of the intellect, always keep your mind fixed on Me.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 59
translation: If you think, 'I shall not fight,' relying on your ego, your determination is vain. Your own nature will compel you to act.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 6
translation: All these activities should be performed without attachment or any expectation of result. They should be performed as a matter of duty, O son of Pritha. That is My final and supreme opinion.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 60
translation: O son of Kunti, bound by your own work which is born of your own nature, that which you do not wish to do out of delusion, you will eventually do even against your will.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 61
translation: The Supreme Lord dwells in the hearts of all living beings, O Arjuna, and by His outward energy, He directs the wanderings of all entities, who are seated as if on a machine.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 65
translation: Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 66
translation: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 7
translation: Prescribed duties should never be renounced. If one gives up his prescribed duties because of illusion, such renunciation is said to be in the mode of ignorance.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 70
translation: And I declare that he who studies this sacred conversation of ours worships Me by his intelligence.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 71
translation: And that person who listens with faith and without envy shall become free from sinful reactions and attain the auspicious abodes of the righteous.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 73
translation: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed, and I have regained my memory through Your grace, O Infallible One. I am now firm, my doubts are gone, and I shall act according to Your word.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 74
translation: Sanjaya said: I have thus heard the conversation of two great souls, Krishna and Arjuna. And so wonderful is that message that my hair is standing on end.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 76
translation: O King, as I repeatedly recall this wondrous and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I am thrilled with joy at every moment.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 77
translation: O King, as I remember that most wonderful form of Lord Krishna, I am struck with even greater wonder, and I rejoice again and again.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 78
translation: Wherever there is Krishna, the master of all mysticism, and wherever there is Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will also certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary power, and morality. That is my

title: Chapter 18, Verse 8
translation: Anyone who gives up prescribed duties as troublesome or out of fear of bodily discomfort is said to have renounced in the mode of passion. Such action never leads to the true fruit of renunciation.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 9
translation: O Arjuna, when one performs their prescribed duty simply because it ought to be done, renouncing all attachment to the action and its fruit, that renunciation is considered to be in the mode of goodne

title: Chapter 2, Verse 31
translation: Furthermore, considering your own specific duty as a warrior, you should not waver. For a warrior, there is no greater good than fighting in a righteous war.

title: Chapter 2, Verse 33
translation: If, however, you refuse to fight this righteous war, abandoning your own duty and reputation, you will certainly incur sin.

title: Chapter 2, Verse 47
translation: You have the right to perform your actions, but never to the results of those actions. Do not consider yourself the cause of the results of your work, and do not become attached to inaction.

title: Chapter 3, Verse 30
translation: Surrendering all your actions unto Me, with your mind focused on the highest self, free from desire and selfishness, fight without any mental fever.

title: Chapter 3, Verse 35
translation: It is better to perform one’s own duty imperfectly than to perform another’s duty perfectly. Even death in the course of one’s own duty is better, for following another’s path is dangerous.

title: Chapter 3, Verse 8
translation: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your physical body cannot be accomplished without action.

title: Chapter 3, Verse 9
translation: Work must be performed as a sacrifice (Yajna), otherwise all actions cause bondage in this world. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your duties for that purpose, completely free from attachment.

title: Chapter 4, Verse 18
translation: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is intelligent among humans. Such a person is situated in a state of harmony, even while performing all kinds of activities.

title: Chapter 4, Verse 24
translation: The act of offering is Brahman, the offering itself is Brahman, it is offered by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. One who sees Brahman in every aspect of action ultimately attains Brahman.

title: Chapter 4, Verse 41
translation: O Dhananjaya, actions do not bind the one who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubts have been cut by knowledge, and who is established in self-awareness.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 1
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Now hear, O son of Pritha, how by practicing yoga with your mind fully attached to Me, and taking exclusive refuge in Me, you can know Me completely, free from all doubt.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 11
translation: I am the strength of the strong, devoid of passion and desire. I am sex life which is not contrary to religious principles, O Lord of the Bharatas (Arjuna).

title: Chapter 7, Verse 13
translation: Deluded by the three modes (goodness, passion and ignorance), the whole world does not know Me, who am above the modes and inexhaustible.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 14
translation: This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 17
translation: Of these, the one who is in full knowledge and who is always engaged in pure devotional service is the best. For I am very dear to him, and he is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 18
translation: All these devotees are undoubtedly magnanimous, but he who is situated in knowledge of Me I consider to be just like My own self. Being engaged in My transcendental service, he is sure to attain Me, t

title: Chapter 7, Verse 20
translation: Those whose intelligence has been stolen by material desires surrender unto demigods and follow the particular rules and regulations of worship according to their own natures.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 23
translation: Men of small intelligence worship the demigods, and their fruits are limited and temporary. Those who worship the demigods go to the planets of the demigods, but My devotees ultimately reach My suprem

title: Chapter 10, Verse 25

translation: One who is always content, self-disciplined, firmly determined, and whose mind and intellect are dedicated to Me, such a devotee is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 15
translation: One by whom the world is not disturbed and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from excessive joy, anger, fear, and agitation, such a person is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 17
translation: One who neither becomes overly joyful nor hates, neither laments nor desires, and who has renounced attachment to both good and bad outcomes, such a devoted person is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 18
translation: One who remains equal toward friend and enemy, balanced in honor and dishonor, and steady in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, free from attachment, such a person is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 19
translation: One who regards praise and criticism equally, who is thoughtful and restrained in speech, content with whatever comes, unattached to fixed possessions or residence, steady in mind and devoted, such a

title: Chapter 12, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me and constantly worship Me with deep faith are considered by Me to be the most perfectly united in yoga.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 20
translation: Those who follow this path of righteous wisdom as described, with faith and with Me as their supreme goal, such devoted individuals are exceedingly dear to Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 3
translation: But those who worship the imperishable, indefinable, unmanifest reality, which is all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, immovable, and eternal, also engage in a path of spiritual discipline.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 4
translation: Those who control their senses, remain balanced in all situations, and are dedicated to the welfare of all beings also ultimately reach Me.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 5
translation: For those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest reality, the path is more difficult. For embodied beings, reaching the unmanifest goal is very challenging.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 6
translation: But those who dedicate all their actions to Me, who regard Me as their supreme goal, and who worship Me while meditating on Me with single-minded focus, follow a path of devotion.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 7
translation: For those whose minds are fully absorbed in Me, O Arjuna, I become their deliverer from the ocean of birth and death, and I quickly lift them out of the cycle of worldly existence.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 8
translation: Fix your mind on Me alone and place your intelligence in Me. Then you will live in Me always, without any doubt.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 9
translation: If you are unable to steadily fix your mind on Me, then try to reach Me through the practice of repeated discipline, O Arjuna.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 1
translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, I wish to understand Prakriti (nature) and Purusha (the enjoyer), as well as the field and the knower of the field, along with knowledge and the object of knowledge.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 10
translation: Non-attachment, absence of entanglement with children, spouse, home, and the rest, and constant even-mindedness amid desirable and undesirable events.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 11
translation: Constant and unalloyed devotion to Me, aspiring to live in a solitary place, and detachment from the general mass of people.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 12
translation: Accepting the importance of self-realization, and the philosophical search for the Absolute Truth—all these I declare to be knowledge, and besides this whatever there may be is ignorance.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 13
translation: I shall now explain that which is to be known, knowing which one tastes the eternal. The Supreme Brahman is beginningless and is said to be neither existent (sat) nor non-existent (asat) in the materi

title: Chapter 13, Verse 15
translation: The Supreme Truth shines through the functions of all the senses, yet is devoid of the senses; He is unattached, yet supports everything; He is free from the modes of nature, yet is the experiencer of

title: Chapter 13, Verse 16
translation: The Supreme Truth exists outside and inside of all living beings, the moving and the nonmoving. Because He is subtle, He is beyond the power of the material senses to see or to know. Although far, far

title: Chapter 13, Verse 17
translation: Although the Supreme Truth appears to be divided among all beings, He is never divided. He is situated as one. Although He is the maintainer of every living entity, it is to be understood that He devo

title: Chapter 13, Verse 18
translation: He is the source of light in all luminous objects. He is beyond the darkness of matter and is unmanifested. He is knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the goal of knowledge. He is situated in every

title: Chapter 13, Verse 19
translation: Thus the field of activities, knowledge, and the knowable have been summarily described by Me. Only My devotees can understand this thoroughly and thus attain to My nature.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field (kshetra), and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field (kshetrajna) by those who understand these things.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 20
translation: Understand that material nature (Prakriti) and the conscious experiencer (Purusha) are both without beginning. Their transformations and the modes of matter are entirely products of material nature.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 21
translation: Material nature (Prakriti) is said to be the cause of all material activities and effects, whereas the conscious entity (Purusha) is the cause of the various experiences of happiness and distress.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 22
translation: The living entity (Purusha) situated in material nature (Prakriti) thus experiences the qualities (gunas) born of material nature. It is this attachment to the modes of nature that is the cause of its

title: Chapter 13, Verse 23
translation: Yet in this body there is another, a transcendental enjoyer, who is the Lord, the supreme proprietor, who exists as the overseer and permitter, and who is known as the Supersoul.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 24
translation: One who understands this philosophy concerning material nature, the living entity, and the interaction of the modes of nature is sure to attain liberation. He will not take birth here again, regardles

title: Chapter 13, Verse 25
translation: Some perceive the Supersoul within themselves through meditation, others through the cultivation of knowledge, and still others through working without fruitive desires.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 29
translation: One who sees the same Supreme Lord situated everywhere in every living being does not degrade himself by his mind and thus reaches the supreme destination.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 3
translation: O scion of Bharata, you should understand that I am also the knower in all bodies, and to understand this body and its knower is called knowledge. That is My opinion.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 30
translation: One who can see that all activities are performed by the body, which is a creation of material nature, and sees that the self does nothing, actually sees.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 32
translation: Those with the vision of eternity can see that the imperishable soul is transcendental, eternal, and beyond the modes of nature. Despite contact with the material body, O Arjuna, the soul neither acts

title: Chapter 13, Verse 33
translation: The sky, due to its subtle nature, although all-pervading, does not mix with anything; similarly, the soul, situated in the body, does not mix with the body.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 35
translation: Those who see with eyes of knowledge the difference between the body and the knower of the body, and who can also understand the process of liberation from bondage in material nature, attain to the su

title: Chapter 13, Verse 4
translation: Now please hear in brief from Me what this field of activity is, what its nature is, what its changes are, where it comes from, who that knower of the field is, and what his influences are.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 5
translation: This knowledge of the field of activities and the knower of activities has been described by various sages in various Vedic hymns. It is especially presented in the Vedanta-sutra with all logic regard

title: Chapter 13, Verse 6
translation: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifest, the ten senses and the mind, and the five objects of the senses.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 7
translation: Desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 8
translation: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity, approaching a bona fide spiritual master, cleanliness, steadiness, and self-control;

title: Chapter 13, Verse 9
translation: Renunciation of the objects of sense gratification, absence of false ego, the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 1
translation: The Supreme Lord said: I shall again reveal to you the supreme wisdom, the best of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages have attained the highest perfection.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 10
translation: Sometimes the mode of goodness becomes prominent, defeating the modes of passion and ignorance, O son of Bharata. Sometimes the mode of passion defeats goodness and ignorance, and at other times ignor

title: Chapter 14, Verse 11
translation: When the light of knowledge illuminates all the gates of the body, then one should know that the mode of goodness is predominant.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 12
translation: O chief of the Bharatas, when the mode of passion increases, the symptoms of greed, intense outward activity, the undertaking of selfish projects, severe restlessness, and uncontrollable craving devel

title: Chapter 14, Verse 13
translation: O son of Kuru, when the mode of ignorance increases, darkness, inactivity, negligence, and delusion are manifested.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 14
translation: When an embodied soul passes away while the mode of goodness is predominant, it attains the pure, higher worlds of those who know the Supreme.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 15
translation: When one dies in the mode of passion, they are born among those attached to fruitive activities; and when one dies in the mode of ignorance, they are born in the deluded species.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 16
translation: The result of righteous action is said to be pure and in the mode of goodness. But action done in the mode of passion results in misery, and action performed in the mode of ignorance results in delusi

title: Chapter 14, Verse 17
translation: From the mode of goodness, real knowledge develops; from the mode of passion, greed develops; and from the mode of ignorance develop negligence, delusion, and foolishness.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 18
translation: Those situated in the mode of goodness go upward; those in the mode of passion remain in the middle; and those in the abominable mode of ignorance go downward.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 19
translation: When one properly sees that in all activities no other performer is at work than these modes of nature, and knows the Supreme who is beyond all these modes, they attain My spiritual nature.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 21
translation: Arjuna inquired: O Lord, by what symptoms is one known who has transcended these three modes of nature? What is their behavior? And how does one transcend these three modes?

title: Chapter 14, Verse 22
translation: The Supreme Lord said: O son of Pandu, one who does not hate illumination, activity, and delusion when they are present, nor longs for them when they disappear...

title: Chapter 14, Verse 23
translation: Seated like an unconcerned witness, one who is not disturbed by the material modes, who remains firm and does not waver, knowing that only the modes are active...

title: Chapter 14, Verse 24
translation: One who is situated in the self and is equal in distress and happiness; who looks upon a clod of dirt, a stone, and a piece of gold with an equal eye; who is equal toward the desirable and the undesir

title: Chapter 14, Verse 25
translation: One who is equal in honor and dishonor, who treats friend and foe alike, and who has renounced all ego-driven undertakings—such a person is said to have transcended the modes of nature.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 26
translation: And one who serves Me with unswerving devotion transcends these three modes of nature and becomes eligible to attain the level of the Supreme.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 27
translation: And I am the basis of the formless Brahman, the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending absolute bliss.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 3
translation: The total material nature is My womb. I place the seed of life within it, and from this, O descendant of Bharata, all living beings are born.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 4
translation: O son of Kunti, of all the forms of life that are born in all species, the great material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 5
translation: Material nature consists of three modes: goodness (sattva), passion (rajas), and ignorance (tamas). These modes condition and bind the eternal, imperishable soul to the physical body, O mighty-armed o

title: Chapter 14, Verse 6
translation: Of these, the mode of goodness, being pure, is illuminating and free from disease. It binds the soul by attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 7
translation: O son of Kunti, know that the mode of passion is characterized by intense craving, born of unlimited desires and longings. It binds the embodied soul through attachment to the results of action.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 8
translation: O son of Bharata, know that the mode of ignorance, born of darkness, is the delusion of all embodied beings. It binds the soul by negligence, laziness, and excessive sleep.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 9
translation: O son of Bharata, the mode of goodness conditions one to happiness; passion conditions one to fruitive action; and ignorance, covering one's knowledge, binds one to negligence and delusion.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 10
translation: The foolish cannot understand how a living entity quits their body, nor can they understand what they enjoy while under the spell of the modes of nature. But one who has the eyes of knowledge can see

title: Chapter 15, Verse 11
translation: The endeavoring yogis, who are situated in self-realization, can clearly see this truth established within themselves. But those whose minds are unpurified and lack self-awareness cannot see it, even

title: Chapter 15, Verse 12
translation: The splendor of the sun, which illuminates the entire world, comes from Me. And the splendor of the moon and the splendor of fire are also from Me.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 13
translation: I enter into each planet, and by My energy, they stay in orbit. I become the moon and thereby supply the juice of life to all vegetables.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 15
translation: I am seated in everyone's heart, and from Me come remembrance, knowledge, and forgetfulness. By all the Vedas, I am to be known. Indeed, I am the compiler of Vedanta, and I am the knower of the Vedas.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 17
translation: Besides these two, there is the greatest living personality, the Supreme Soul, the imperishable Lord Himself, who has entered the three worlds and is maintaining them.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 18
translation: Because I am transcendental, beyond both the perishable and the imperishable, and because I am the greatest, I am celebrated both in the world and in the Vedas as that Supreme Person.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 19
translation: Whoever knows Me as the Supreme Person, without doubting, is the knower of everything. He, therefore, engages himself in wholehearted service to Me, O son of Bharata.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 3
translation: The real form of this tree cannot be perceived in this world. No one can understand where it ends, where it begins, or where its foundation is. But with determination, one must cut down this strongly

title: Chapter 15, Verse 5
translation: Those who are free from false prestige, illusion, and the fault of attachment, who are eternally situated in the understanding of the self, who are freed from selfish desires, and who are liberated fr

title: Chapter 15, Verse 7
translation: The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 8
translation: When the living entity (the lord of the body) acquires a body or departs from one, he takes the mind and the senses with him, just as the wind carries fragrances from their sources.

title: Chapter 15, Verse 9
translation: Taking a new body, the living entity acquires a specific set of ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose, all clustered around the mind. Through these, it experiences a particular set of sense objects.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 1
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Fearlessness; purification of one's existence; cultivation of spiritual knowledge; charity; self-control; performance of sacrifice; study of the Vedas; austerity; and simplicity

title: Chapter 16, Verse 10
translation: Taking shelter of insatiable lust and absorbed in the conceit of pride and false prestige, the demoniac, thus disillusioned, are always sworn to unclean work, attracted by the impermanent.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 13
translation: The demoniac person thinks: 'So much wealth do I have today, and I will gain more according to my schemes. So much is mine now, and it will increase in the future, more and more.'

title: Chapter 16, Verse 14
translation: The demoniac person thinks: 'This enemy has been slain by me, and I shall kill the others also! I am the lord of all. I am the enjoyer. I am perfect, powerful and happy.'

title: Chapter 16, Verse 16
translation: Thus perplexed by various anxieties and bound by a network of illusions, they become too strongly attached to sense enjoyment and fall down into hell.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 17
translation: Self-complacent and always impudent, deluded by wealth and false prestige, they sometimes perform sacrifices in name only, for show, without following any rules or regulations.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 18
translation: Bewildered by false ego, strength, pride, lust and anger, the demoniac person becomes envious of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in his own body and in as well as in the bodies of

title: Chapter 16, Verse 19
translation: Those who are envious and mischievous, who are the lowest among men, I perpetually cast into the ocean of material existence, into various demoniac species of life.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 20
translation: Attaining repeated birth amongst the species of demoniac life, O son of Kunti, such persons can never approach Me. Gradually they sink down to the most abominable type of existence.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 21
translation: There are three gates leading to this hell—lust, anger and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 22
translation: The man who has escaped these three gates of hell, O son of Kunti, performs acts conducive to self-realization and thus gradually attains the supreme destination.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 23
translation: He who discards scriptural injunctions and acts according to his own whims attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 5
translation: The divine qualities are considered conducive to liberation, whereas the demoniac qualities lead to bondage. Do not grieve, O son of Pandu, for you are born with the divine qualities.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 6
translation: O son of Pritha, in this world there are two kinds of created beings. One is called the divine and the other demoniac. I have already explained at length the divine qualities. Now hear from Me of the

title: Chapter 16, Verse 7
translation: Those who are demoniac do not know what is to be done and what is not to be done. Neither cleanliness nor proper behavior nor truth is found in them.

title: Chapter 16, Verse 9
translation: Following such conclusions, the demoniac persons, who are lost to themselves and who have no intelligence, engage in unbeneficial, horrible works meant to destroy the world.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 10
translation: Food prepared more than three hours before being eaten, food which is tasteless, decomposed and putrid, and food consisting of remnants and untouchable things is dear to those in the mode of ignorance

title: Chapter 17, Verse 11
translation: Of sacrifices, the sacrifice performed according to the directions of scripture, as a matter of duty, by those who desire no reward, is of the nature of goodness.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 14
translation: Austerity of the body consists in worship of the Supreme Lord, the wise, the spiritual master, and superiors like the father and mother, and in cleanliness, simplicity, celibacy and nonviolence.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 15
translation: Austerity of speech consists in speaking words that are truthful, pleasing, beneficial, and not agitating to others, and also in regularly reciting Vedic literature.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 16
translation: And satisfaction, simplicity, gravity, self-control and purification of one's existence are the austerities of the mind.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 17
translation: This threefold austerity, performed with supreme faith by men who do not desire rewards and are in union with the Divine, is said to be in the mode of goodness.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 21
translation: But charity performed with the expectation of some return, or with a desire for fruits, or in a grudging mood, is said to be in the mode of passion.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 23
translation: From the beginning of creation, the three words 'Om Tat Sat' have been used to indicate the Supreme Ultimate Reality. These three symbolic representations were used by the knowers of the Absolute whil

title: Chapter 17, Verse 24
translation: Therefore, by uttering the word 'Om', the acts of sacrifice, charity and penance, as enjoined in the scriptures, are always begun by the students of the Absolute.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 25
translation: One should perform various kinds of sacrifice, penance and charity with the word 'Tat' and without desiring the results. Such activities are performed by those who seek liberation from material entang

title: Chapter 17, Verse 3
translation: O descendant of Bharata, the faith of all beings is in accordance with their nature. A person is made of their faith; as their faith is, so they are.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 4
translation: Those in the mode of goodness worship the demigods; those in the mode of passion worship the demons; and those in the mode of ignorance worship ghosts and spirits.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 6
translation: Senselessly torturing the elements of the body and also Me who dwells within it—know such people to be of demoniac resolve.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 7
translation: Even the food each person prefers is of three kinds, according to the three modes of material nature. The same is true of sacrifices, austerities and charity. Now hear of the distinctions between them

title: Chapter 17, Verse 8
translation: Foods that increase longevity, virtue, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction are characteristic of the mode of goodness. Such foods are juicy, fatty, wholesome, and pleasing to the heart.

title: Chapter 17, Verse 9
translation: Foods that are too bitter, too sour, salty, hot, pungent, dry and burning are liked by those in the mode of passion. Such foods cause distress, misery and disease.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 1
translation: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, I wish to understand the true nature of renunciation (sannyasa) and of detachment (tyaga), and the distinction between the two, O Hrishikesha, killer of the Kesi demon

title: Chapter 18, Verse 13
translation: O mighty-armed Arjuna, learn from Me the five factors for the accomplishment of all actions, as declared in the Sankhya philosophy, which is the ultimate conclusion of all action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 15
translation: Whatever right or wrong action a man performs by body, mind or speech, is caused by these five factors.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 16
translation: Therefore, one who thinks himself the only doer, not considering the five factors, is certainly not very intelligent and cannot see things as they are.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 17
translation: One who is free from the ego of being the doer, and whose intelligence is not entangled, even though he may slay all these people, he does not kill, nor is he bound by the consequences of the action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 18
translation: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower—these three are the motivating forces of action. The instrument, the action, and the doer—these three are the constituents of action.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 19
translation: According to the three different modes of material nature, there are three kinds of knowledge, action, and performer of action. Now hear of them from Me.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Giving up activities based on material desire is what learned men call sannyasa (renunciation). And giving up the results of all activities is what the wise call tyaga (detachme

title: Chapter 18, Verse 25
translation: That action which is undertaken out of delusion, completely disregarding future consequences, loss, injury to others, and one's own capability, is said to be in the mode of ignorance (Tamasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 27
translation: The worker who is attached to work and the fruits of work, desiring to enjoy those fruits, and who is greedy, always envious, impure, and moved by joy and sorrow, is said to be a worker in the mode of

title: Chapter 18, Verse 28
translation: The worker who is undisciplined, vulgar, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, morose and procrastinating is said to be a worker in the mode of ignorance (Tamasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 29
translation: O winner of wealth, now please listen as I tell you in detail of the three kinds of understanding and determination according to the three modes of material nature.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 30
translation: O son of Pritha, that understanding by which one knows what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, what is to be feared and what is not to be feared, what is binding and what is liberating, i

title: Chapter 18, Verse 31
translation: O son of Pritha, that understanding which cannot distinguish between right and wrong, between action that should be done and action that should not be done, is in the mode of passion (Rajasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 32
translation: That understanding which considers irreligion to be religion and religion to be irreligion, under the spell of illusion and darkness, and strives always in the wrong direction, O Partha, is in the mod

title: Chapter 18, Verse 33
translation: O son of Pritha, that determination which is unswerving, which is sustained with steadfastness by yoga practice, and which thus controls the activities of the mind, life and senses, is in the mode of

title: Chapter 18, Verse 34
translation: But that determination by which one holds fast to duty, pleasure, and wealth, desiring the fruits of actions out of intense attachment, O Partha, is in the mode of passion (Rajasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 35
translation: O son of Pritha, that determination which cannot go beyond dreaming, fearfulness, lamentation, moroseness, and illusion—that unintelligent determination is in the mode of ignorance (Tamasic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 37
translation: That happiness which is like poison in the beginning but like nectar in the end, and which arises from the purification of one’s own intelligence, is said to be in the mode of goodness (Sattvic).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 4
translation: O best of the Bharatas, now hear My conclusive judgment concerning renunciation. O tiger among men, renunciation is declared in the scriptures to be of three kinds.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 40
translation: There is no being on earth, or even among the demigods in the higher planetary systems, who is freed from these three modes born of material nature.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 42
translation: Peacefulness, self-control, austerity, purity, tolerance, honesty, knowledge, wisdom and religiousness—these are the natural qualities by which the Brahmins work.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 45
translation: By following his qualities of work, every man can become perfect. Now please hear from Me how this can be done.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 5
translation: Acts of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up; they must be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity and penance purify even the great souls.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 51
translation: Being purified by intelligence and controlling the mind with determination, giving up the objects of sense gratification, and casting aside attachment and hatred...

title: Chapter 18, Verse 52
translation: Resorting to secluded places, eating light, controlling speech, body and mind, ever engaged in meditation and taking refuge in dispassion...

title: Chapter 18, Verse 53
translation: One who has abandoned false ego, false strength, arrogance, desire, anger, and possessiveness—who is free from the notion of 'mine' and is peaceful—is fit for realizing the Supreme (Brahman).

title: Chapter 18, Verse 54
translation: One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments or desires to have anything. He is equally disposed toward every living entity

title: Chapter 18, Verse 55
translation: Only through devotion can one come to know Me in truth—who and what I am. Having known Me in truth, one then enters into My being.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 57
translation: Mentally dedicating all your actions to Me, regarding Me as the Supreme Goal and taking shelter of the yoga of the intellect, always keep your mind fixed on Me.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 58
translation: If you become conscious of Me, you will pass over all the obstacles of life by My grace. If, however, you do not act in such consciousness but act through false ego, not hearing Me, you will be lost.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 6
translation: All these activities should be performed without attachment or any expectation of result. They should be performed as a matter of duty, O son of Pritha. That is My final and supreme opinion.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 61
translation: The Supreme Lord dwells in the hearts of all living beings, O Arjuna, and by His outward energy, He directs the wanderings of all entities, who are seated as if on a machine.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 62
translation: Surrender unto Him utterly, O descendant of Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 63
translation: Thus I have explained to you knowledge still more confidential. Deliberate on this fully, and then do what you wish to do.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 64
translation: Because you are My very dear friend, I am speaking to you My supreme instruction, the most confidential knowledge of all. Hear this from Me, for it is for your benefit.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 65
translation: Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 66
translation: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 67
translation: This secret knowledge should never be explained to those who are not austere, or devoted, or engaged in service, nor to one who is envious of Me.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 68
translation: For one who explains this supreme secret to the devotees, pure devotional service is guaranteed, and at the end he will come back to Me.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 70
translation: And I declare that he who studies this sacred conversation of ours worships Me by his intelligence.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 71
translation: And that person who listens with faith and without envy shall become free from sinful reactions and attain the auspicious abodes of the righteous.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 72
translation: O son of Pritha, O conqueror of wealth, have you heard this with a concentrated mind? Has your delusion born of ignorance been dispelled?

title: Chapter 18, Verse 73
translation: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed, and I have regained my memory through Your grace, O Infallible One. I am now firm, my doubts are gone, and I shall act according to Your word.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 75
translation: By the mercy of Vyasa, I have heard these most confidential talks directly from the master of all mysticism, Krishna, who was speaking personally to Arjuna.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 76
translation: O King, as I repeatedly recall this wondrous and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I am thrilled with joy at every moment.

translation: One who knows Me as unborn, without beginning, and as the supreme Lord of all worlds, such a person among mortals is free from delusion and is released from all sinful reactions.

title: Chapter 12, Verse 2
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me and constantly worship Me with deep faith are considered by Me to be the most perfectly united in yoga.

title: Chapter 13, Verse 15
translation: The Supreme Truth shines through the functions of all the senses, yet is devoid of the senses; He is unattached, yet supports everything; He is free from the modes of nature, yet is the experiencer of

title: Chapter 13, Verse 7
translation: Desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions—all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.

title: Chapter 14, Verse 10
translation: Sometimes the mode of goodness becomes prominent, defeating the modes of passion and ignorance, O son of Bharata. Sometimes the mode of passion defeats goodness and ignorance, and at other times ignor

title: Chapter 17, Verse 27
translation: The state of steadfastness in sacrifice, penance and charity is also called 'Sat,' and any work performed for the sake of the Supreme is also designated as 'Sat.'

title: Chapter 18, Verse 5
translation: Acts of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up; they must be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity and penance purify even the great souls.

title: Chapter 18, Verse 65
translation: Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.

title: Chapter 2, Verse 14
translation: O son of Kunti, the contact between the senses and their objects gives rise to fleeting perceptions of happiness and distress. These are non-permanent, coming and going like the winter and summer seas

title: Chapter 2, Verse 15
translation: O best among men, the person who is not disturbed by happiness and distress and is steady in both is certainly eligible for liberation.

title: Chapter 2, Verse 38
translation: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. Then engage in battle. By doing so, you will not incur sin.

title: Chapter 2, Verse 38
translation: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. Then engage in battle. By doing so, you will not incur sin.

title: Chapter 2, Verse 70
translation: Just as rivers enter the ever-full and steady ocean without disturbing it, in the same way all desires enter the person who remains steady. Such a person attains peace, not the one who constantly long

title: Chapter 2, Verse 71
translation: A person who abandons all selfish desires, moves through life free from craving, without possessiveness and without ego, attains peace.

title: Chapter 3, Verse 7
translation: But one who controls the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, and engages the organs of action in Karma-yoga without attachment, is far superior.

title: Chapter 4, Verse 26
translation: Some offer the senses such as hearing into the fire of self-control, while others offer sound and other sense objects into the fire of the senses.

title: Chapter 4, Verse 29

title: Chapter 7, Verse 17
translation: Of these, the one who is in full knowledge and who is always engaged in pure devotional service is the best. For I am very dear to him, and he is dear to Me.

title: Chapter 7, Verse 28
translation: Persons who have acted piously in previous lives and in this life and whose sinful actions are completely eradicated are freed from the dualities of delusion, and they engage themselves in My service

title: Chapter 8, Verse 14
translation: For one who always remembers Me without deviation, I am easy to obtain, O son of Pritha, because of his constant engagement in devotional service.

title: Chapter 8, Verse 22
translation: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is greater than all, is attainable by unalloyed devotion. Although He is present in His abode, He is all-pervading, and everything is situated within Him.

title: Chapter 9, Verse 12
translation: Those who are thus bewildered embrace a destructive and ignorant nature. In this deluded state, all their hopes, all their actions, and all their knowledge become entirely vain and meaningless.

title: Chapter 9, Verse 14
translation: Always glorifying Me, striving with firm determination, and bowing down before Me, these great souls perpetually worship Me with devotion.

title: Chapter 9, Verse 2
